clue.text: Shock vote for right then opposition leader winning

parts.note: to elect is to vote someone in

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of opposition is used

parts.note: winning in the sense of charming or appealing, so cute

explanation.surface: A ballot swings to the right and the opposition chief's victory comes as a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like a noun about the vote result, but it is a verb meaning to kill or jolt with electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill or injure with an electric current is to give a fatal electric shock.

clue.text: Goes over catalogues

definitions.meaning: a ship that ... leans over to one side
catalogues as a verb means records in order, itemises

explanation.definitionFit: Lists means both leans over, as a ship, and enumerates items.

clue.text: Caught old band covering Queen set

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the band word wraps around the queen word

parts.note: a tie is a band or bond
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A veteran rock group arrested while playing a royal set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' is the container signal; 'set' looks like part of a band's gig but is the definition, a clique.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group of people, a clique or set.

clue.text: Shoots unedited film scenes

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means dashes, shoots along
the first prints of a day's filming are called dailies

explanation.definitionFit: Rushes means hurries and also the unedited daily prints of film footage.

clue.text: Regular criminals beat time

parts.note: cons are convicts
to tan someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: Lawbreakers routinely do their time.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant means steady and unchanging, like something regular.

clue.text: Provider of digital protection?

parts.note: digital sounds like computing security, but it refers to fingers, and the item guards a finger while sewing

explanation.surface: Advertising for a cybersecurity company.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cap worn on a fingertip shields it from the needle when sewing.

clue.text: Political extremists enact ruling if wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are put in the wrong order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Radicals would pass a law if it were mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the wild minority of any political movement holding extreme views.

clue.text: Artist on ball capturing single light

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician

indicators.note: one word holds the other within it

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A painter at a ball catches a lone gleam of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' is the container signal; 'on' is a link, the artist sitting above the rest in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance is bright light or glow given off by something.

clue.text: Garage to stop Reliant rattling…

indicators.note: rattling suggests something shaken up, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Pull into a garage to stop a rattling Reliant car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattling' rearranges TOSTOPRELIANT. The Reliant Robin was a British three-wheeled car, which suits a garage.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage can be a filling station selling fuel.

clue.text: Worked up seeing classy pin-up embracing pole

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: one word holding another inside it, as in a hug

parts.note: a pin-up is a favourite, a pet
S is the abbreviation for the South pole

explanation.surface: Someone gets agitated looking at a glamorous poster girl hugging a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts S inside PET. U for upper-class is a Nancy Mitford-era convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upset is being agitated or emotionally worked up.

clue.text: Group deny act is rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb or adjective suggests something badly done, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A protest that denying an act is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndicate is a group of people or firms combining for a common business purpose.

clue.text: Sailor posted around globe for soaking

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: the sending word goes round the sphere word

parts.note: posted a letter means sent it
an orb is a globe

explanation.surface: A seaman mails something round the world to have it soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal: the globe goes inside the posted word, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absorbent takes up liquid, so it is suited to soaking things up.

clue.text: Water finally put on cheese plant

indicators.note: the closing letter is placed after the cheese, added on to it

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of water

explanation.surface: Instructions to sprinkle water on a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'plant' look like part of a kitchen scene; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The brier, or briar, is a thorny shrub such as the wild rose.

clue.text: One's prosecuted and released

parts.note: one is I, and the possessive adds S
to sue someone is to take them to court

explanation.surface: Someone is taken to court and then set free.
explanation.definitionFit: Something issued has been put out or released to the public.

clue.text: …start to service engine cover with frown

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a cowling is the removable cover over an aircraft engine

explanation.surface: Beginning to service the engine, the mechanic frowns at its cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Scowling means looking angry or displeased, wearing a frown.

clue.text: Assume name nearly everyone cursed

parts.note: to infer is to deduce or assume

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Presuming a name to be damned by nearly the whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal, literally hellish, is used colloquially to mean damned or cursed.

clue.text: Get more demented say, seeing puzzle

parts.note: to get mad is to be mad, so get stands for be
wilder means crazier, given here as an example of being more demented

explanation.surface: Someone becoming more unhinged, finding it all baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer split after two letters to hear the phrase about becoming crazier.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder someone is to confuse or perplex them.

clue.text: Depressed after fellow came out

indicators.note: the depressed word comes after the fellow letter

parts.note: depressed in the physical sense of pushed down, lowered

explanation.surface: Someone felt low after a friend revealed their sexuality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came out' suggests a personal revelation, but it means bloomed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that flowered has come out into bloom.

clue.text: Endless tears over a red inflammation

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits above the rest
without its ends, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: Che Guevara is a stock example of a Red, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: Unending tears over red swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is pain in the ear, often from an inflammation or infection.

clue.text: The French try to get fashionable

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a test is a try or trial

explanation.surface: The French attempt to be trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest styles are the most up-to-date and modish ones.

clue.text: Briefly America's ally inside NATO, perhaps

indicators.note: the ally word goes within the short form

parts.note: AM is a short form of American
a crony is a close companion or ally

explanation.surface: In a nutshell, America's partner within the NATO alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is the container signal; 'Briefly' shortens the word for American.
explanation.definitionFit: NATO is formed from initial letters and pronounced as a word, an example of the type.

clue.text: Stands high on board ship

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
high means tall

explanation.surface: A tall structure on a steamer's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the container signal, a common convention for going inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Market stalls are stands, booths selling goods.

clue.text: Individual doing little except relax initially

definitions.text: Individual doing little except relax initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A person who does nothing but take it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the five words before 'initially' spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout who does little but relax is a typical lazy person.

clue.text: Painter pretentiously about to clarify

indicators.note: about here means around or in, so the answer sits within the two words

explanation.surface: An artist pompously attempts to explain his work.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'Painter pretentiously'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret something is to explain its meaning, to make it clear.

clue.text: Scouting about company with new leader

parts.note: re means about

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A scouting troop gets a fresh leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Recon is short for reconnaissance, military scouting of territory.

clue.text: Terribly eager to finish race?

parts.note: the race reads like a running contest, but it is a people, and wanting to finish one off is a horrific desire

explanation.surface: A competitor desperate to get to the end of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intent on destroying an entire race or ethnic group has murderous, exterminating aims.

clue.text: Eaten by Mexican, a choice dish

indicators.note: the answer is swallowed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Mexican diner tucks into a choice dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla chip topped with cheese is a classic Tex-Mex snack served as a dish.

clue.text: About time to embrace cocky blokes for stimulation

indicators.note: the outer letters hug the inner phrase

parts.note: re means about or concerning
fresh means cheeky or cocky
men are blokes

explanation.surface: It is time to hug brash chaps as a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts FRESHMEN between RE and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Food and drink are a refreshment, reviving and stimulating the body.
